newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real ends flat after see-saw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real ends flat after see-saw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real see-sawed to end flat at 1.0305 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market on higher dollar inflows caused by an increase in export contracts, dealers said.

In the morning session the local currency fell a maximum of 0.09 percent to 1.0314 per greenback due to an excess of reais in the market. But it pared losses to end flat as dollars poured into the market, dealers said.

Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Wednesday deficit of around $13 million. In the floating exchange rate market, the real also closed steady at 1.0353 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real dropped 0.93 percent to end at 1.085 per greenback.
